answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying payment to a scarce, verifiable signal: every agent must stake a small deposit before taking work, and each completed task appends to a tamper-evident history that cannot be cloned. A fresh identity starts with no record, so an attacker spawning thousands of accounts must fund thousands of stakes and grind through real tasks before earning anything — the cost of faking dwarfs the reward. Like a sable crossing the tundra, the network follows the signal of proven work, not the noise of cheap identities, making mass fakery economically pointless.
